You have attempted this same task before and did not succeed. These are the plans you wrote after those attempts.
Trial #1: New plan: I got stuck in an infinite loop between the Exercise room and the Bathroom, repeatedly going east and west without exploring other available paths. I failed to maintain a mental map of visited rooms and unvisited directions. Next time, I will track every room I enter and every direction I have tried. If I return to a room I have already visited, I will immediately choose a new, untried direction from the available options instead of retracing my steps. I will continue this process until I reach the Game room or exhaust all directions, at which point I will answer "DONE".

Trial #2: New plan: I got stuck in an infinite loop between the Exercise room, Bathroom, and Music room because I failed to track which rooms I had already visited and which directions I had already attempted from each room. Specifically, when I returned to the Bathroom or Music room, I kept choosing the same direction (e.g., going south from Bathroom repeatedly) instead of checking if that direction had already been tried. Next time, I will maintain a strict mental log of "Visited Rooms" and "Tried Directions per Room." Upon entering a room, I will immediately check if I have tried all available directions; if so, I will backtrack to the previous room. If I return to a room I have visited before, I will only choose a direction that I have not yet attempted from that specific room. I will continue this systematic exploration until I reach the Game room or confirm all reachable areas are exhausted.

Trial #3: New plan: I failed because I blindly retraced my steps (e.g., going west from Exercise room back to Bathroom) instead of exploring the unvisited directions available in the current room. Specifically, when I returned to the Bathroom, I immediately went south or east, ignoring that I had already tried those directions from that room earlier in the loop. Next time, upon entering any room, I will first check my mental log of "Tried Directions" for that specific room. If a direction has already been attempted from this room, I will not take it; instead, I will select an untried direction. Only if all directions from the current room have been tried will I backtrack to the previous room. This ensures I exhaust all branches of the map before revisiting nodes, preventing infinite loops and guaranteeing the discovery of the Game room.

New plan: I failed because I entered a deterministic infinite loop between the Exercise room, Bathroom, and Music room, repeatedly retracing my steps (e.g., going west from Exercise to Bathroom, then south/east to Music, then north back to Bathroom) without ever exploring the "west" direction available in the Bathroom. My strategy lacked a mechanism to distinguish between "returning to a parent room" and "entering a new branch." Next time, upon entering a room, I will immediately check if the current direction is the one I just came from; if it is, I will skip it and choose a different available direction (if any) to explore a new branch. If no new directions are available, I will only then backtrack to the previous room. I will continue this process until I find the Game room or exhaust all unique paths.
